## Simulating a Wiener process model 

```{r}
#| echo: false 
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggdist)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

set.seed(51)
```

Source: https://sites.me.ucsb.edu/~moehlis/APC591/tutorials/tutorial7/node2.html 

A standard Wiener process^[often called Brownian motion] on the interval $[0, T]$ is a random variable $W(t)$ that depends continuously on $t in [0, T]$ and satisifes the following: 

- $W(0) = 0$ 
- For $0 <= s < t <= T$, 
$$W(t) - W(s) \sim \sqrt{t-s} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$
- For $0 <= s < t < u < v <= T$, $W(t) - W(s)$ and $W(v) - W(u)$ are independent. 

To make things easier on a computer, we discretize the Wiener process with a timestamp $d t$ as $$d W \sim \sqrt{d t} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$ 

```{r}
# params
T <- 1
N <- 500              # number of steps
dt <- T / N
times <- seq(0, T, length.out = N + 1)
paths <- 50

# storage (rows = paths, cols = time steps including t=0)
W <- matrix(0, nrow = paths, ncol = N + 1)
hit_idx <- rep(NA_integer_, paths)  # index of first hit (NA if never hits)

for (p in seq_len(paths)) {
  for (i in 2:(N + 1)) {
    dW <- sqrt(dt) * rnorm(1)
    W[p, i] <- W[p, i - 1] + dW
    if (W[p, i] >= 1 || W[p, i] <= -1) {
      hit_idx[p] <- i
      # copy the absorbing value forward
      if (i < (N + 1)) W[p, (i + 1):(N + 1)] <- W[p, i]
      break
    }
  }
  # if never hit, W[p, ] is already fully filled
}

# convert to long dataframe for ggplot
df <- tibble(
  path = rep(seq_len(paths), each = N + 1),
  time = rep(times, times = paths),
  W = as.vector(t(W))    # t(W) so we stack path-wise
)
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true 
df <- df %>% mutate(path = factor(path))

# quick plot: many thin lines (no legend), dashed horizontal at ±1
ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = W, group = path, color = path)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Simulated paths with absorbing boundaries at ±1",
       x = "time", y = "W(t)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# compute first-passage time per path
first_passage <- df %>%
  group_by(path) %>%
  summarize(
    hit_time = ifelse(any(abs(W) >= 1),
                      time[which(abs(W) >= 1)[1]],
                      NA_real_)  # NA if never hit
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# look at summary
summary(first_passage$hit_time)
```

```{r}
ggplot(first_passage, aes(x = hit_time)) +
  stat_halfeye() + 
  # geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of First-Passage Times (|W| ≥ 1)",
    x = "First passage time",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

## Comprison to the `RWiener` package

- [Reference manual](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RWiener/RWiener.pdf) 


```{r}
library(RWiener)
dat <- rwiener(100,3,.25,.5,0.8)

dat %>% count(resp)
```
